title.narrative: Togo Transport Connectivity and Logistics Improvement Program

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the Togo Transport Connectivity and Logistics Improvement Program (PASLT) is to enhance safe urban mobility and logistics systems efficiency in the Greater Lome Metropolitan Area, and support safe climate resilient connectivity to selected regions with high agricultural potential in Togo. This PDO translates into four interrelated outcome dimensions, which together reflect the territorial connectivity approach underpinning the project design.Outcome 1: Improved Urban Mobility Efficiency in Greater LomeThe project aims to improve the efficiency, reliability, and predictability of urban mobility within the Greater Lome Metropolitan Area (GLMA), particularly along priority corridors that experience high congestion and conflicts between urban traffic and freight movements. Targeted investments under the Port City Integration and Urban Mobility component address critical bottlenecks around the Port of Lome, optimize freight circulation, improve road condition and traffic management, and enhance last mile connectivity between urban areas, logistics zones, and the port interface.Improvements in urban mobility efficiency are expected to reduce travel times, lower congestion related economic costs, and improve accessibility for urban residents and economic operators. These outcomes contribute directly to national competitiveness and the functioning of the port–city–hinterland logistics chain.PDO indicator(s) linked to this outcome:- Direct users that benefit from improved access to sustainable transport infrastructure and services (Number of people) [CRI]- Average travel time on Lome ring road urban corridor (Minutes)Outcome 2: Enhanced Logistics Efficiency in Greater LomeThe project strengthens logistics efficiency in Greater Lome by improving port–industrial and port–urban connectivity, with a particular focus on the Port of Lome (PAL) – Plateforme Industrielle d’Adetikope (PIA) corridor. The rehabilitation and operationalization of the PAL–PIA railway, combined with complementary urban access and traffic management investments, are expected to reduce freight transport time and costs, enable modal shift from road to rail, and reduce truck congestion in dense urban areas.These improvements are critical to enhancing the performance of the logistics ecosystem in Greater Lome, supporting industrial activity at the PIA, facilitating transit traffic to and from landlocked countries, and reinforcing Togo's role as a regional logistics hub.PDO indicator(s) linked to this outcome:- Transport costs between the PAL and the PIA for 20ft container (Amount in USD)- Average cargo dwell time at the Port of Lome (Days)Outcome 3: Enhanced Climate Resilience of the Road NetworkAcross both urban and rural contexts, the project seeks to enhance the climate resilience of the road network by rehabilitating and upgrading road infrastructure to climate resilient standards. Interventions incorporate improved drainage, flood protection, slope stabilization, and fit for purpose design to ensure that roads remain serviceable under current and projected climate conditions, particularly during extreme rainfall and flooding events.By improving the resilience of transport infrastructure, the project aims to reduce climate related service disruptions, protect public investment, and ensure continuity of access to markets, services, and logistics corridors. This outcome cuts across the entire PDO and supports long term sustainability and risk reduction.PDO indicator(s) linked to this outcome:- Project-supported road network that is passable year-round (Kilometers)Outcome 4: Improved Road Access to Targeted High Potential Agricultural ZonesThe project improves physical access between high potential agricultural production zones—particularly Zones d’Amenagement Agricole Planifie (ZAAPs)—and markets, aggregation points, and logistics nodes. Rehabilitation of feeder, secondary, and selected national roads ensures more reliable, all season connectivity, reducing travel times, transport costs, and post harvest losses for agricultural producers.Improved road access is expected to strengthen the integration of rural production areas into domestic and regional markets, facilitate input supply and output evacuation, and enhance the enabling conditions for private investment along agricultural value chains. This outcome supports agricultural productivity, rural livelihoods, and territorial inclusion, especially in northern and climate vulnerable regions.PDO indicator(s) linked to this outcome:- ZAAPs connected with all-season road access (Number)
The Project Development Objective is to enhance (i) efficient urban mobility and logistics in Greater Lome, and (ii) climate- resilient road access in targeted high-potential agricultural zones.
